description: Cross-binding conformance for the three model constructs no evaluator in the executing bindings runs: a CONTINUOUS EVENT (`continuous_events`), a DISCRETE EVENT (`discrete_events`) and an IMPLICIT EQUATION (an equation whose LHS is an expression rather than a bare unknown, an indexed unknown, `D(unknown)` or `ic(unknown)`). Before issues #264 and #356 they validated and were then silently dropped by most evaluators: the event never fired and the residual was never solved, so a run reported a number the document does not describe. The decision this category pins is REFUSAL: an evaluator that cannot run the construct MUST fail the build with the diagnostic `unsupported_construct` (esm-spec §9.6.6), and the message MUST name the construct and the evaluator. It pins no numbers. The `control` case is the discrete-event array document with its event removed; it takes the same array evaluator and MUST still run, which is what attributes the refusals to the construct. The coupled case puts the array continuous-event model next to a second model, which some bindings build through a different route. Julia's ModelingToolkit export runs both kinds of event and hands implicit equations to `mtkcompile`, so it is outside this category; Go and TypeScript do not simulate and only register the code.
